memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Bring his sons and dress them in tunics. Anoint them just as you anointed their father, so that they may serve me as priests. Their anointing will be to a priesthood that will continue throughout their generations.'" - Exod 40:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The sons were dressed and anointed "just as you anointed their father." Same washing, same garments, same anointing. No lesser version for the next generation.

God was thinking beyond Aaron. This priesthood was to continue through the generations — a work that would outlast the man who began it.

That perspective is worth borrowing. We are all tempted to think only about our own season of usefulness. God thinks in generations. Paul told Timothy to entrust what he had learned to reliable people who would be qualified to teach others (2 Tim 2:2).

Who is being anointed after you? Who is learning from how you pray, give, forgive, and handle disappointment?

The Aaronic priesthood did continue for centuries — but it also had a limitation. Those priests died and had to be replaced, one after another. Hebrews makes the contrast: there were many priests because death prevented them from continuing, but because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood (Heb 7:23-24).

Aaron's line needed constant replacement. Christ needs none. And in Him, we are all brought into a royal priesthood (1 Pet 2:9) that will never require a successor.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who is learning from you, whether you intended it or not?
2. Are you investing in anything that will outlast you?
3. What does it mean that Christ's priesthood never needs replacing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, let Your work in me outlast me. Show me who to pour into for the next generation. Amen.
